analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: The cleanest technical setup in the market right now, and the fundamentals earned it — a bank at new highs on 34% EPS growth still trading at 11.8x forward earnings.

financials.summary: Bank of America's last full fiscal year was defined by net interest income recovery. As the deposit-repricing pressure of the prior tightening cycle eased and the securities portfolio rolled into higher-yielding paper, net interest margin expanded meaningfully — the mechanism behind the 34% EPS growth the scan reports. Trading and investment banking added a strong second engine as capital-markets activity reopened, while credit costs stayed contained: consumer charge-offs normalised toward pre-pandemic levels rather than deteriorating, and commercial-real-estate reserves proved adequate. Capital generation was strong enough to support both a dividend increase and sustained buybacks, and the balance sheet crossed the year comfortably above regulatory CET1 minimums. The reason the market is re-rating the stock is that this is operating leverage, not a one-off: expenses grew slower than revenue.

Continued digital-banking share gains, keeping cost-to-serve trending down

journey_52w.summary: A textbook year-long base-and-breakout. BAC traded as low as 43.96 and closed the latest session at 62.48 — a 42% advance off the low — and it did so in stages rather than a single spike. The stock spent much of the year building a five-contraction consolidation as the market debated whether bank earnings could grow without rate cuts; each successive pullback was shallower, compressing to a final 2.5% range. The resolution came as investors rotated out of high-multiple growth and into cash-flow-at-a-low-multiple, exactly the rotation now visible across the whole leaderboard. It closed this session 0.2% from its 52-week high with RSI at only 61.7 and its RS line at new highs, which is the signature of a stock being accumulated rather than chased.

analyses.name: U.S. Bancorp
analyses.verdict: The cheapest quality name in the market's leadership group at 11.0x forward earnings — and the one TradingView rates most highly.

financials.summary: U.S. Bancorp's last full year was a story of digesting the Union Bank acquisition and returning to organic growth. Integration costs that had weighed on prior-period results rolled off, revealing the underlying earnings power of a franchise with one of the best efficiency ratios among large regionals. Net interest income improved as funding costs stabilised and the loan book repriced. The fee businesses — payments processing, trust and investment management, mortgage banking — are unusually large as a share of revenue for a regional bank, and they provided ballast that pure spread lenders lacked. Credit quality remained a relative strength, with charge-offs below peer averages. Capital rebuilt steadily through the year, restoring flexibility for buybacks after the acquisition-related drawdown.

journey_52w.summary: USB travelled from 42.40 to 63.94 over the year — a 51% advance, the strongest of the large banks — but the character of the move was steady rather than dramatic. The low came when the market was still penalising the stock for Union Bank integration costs and questioning regional-bank funding stability in the aftermath of the 2023 stress episode. As those costs rolled off and deposits proved sticky, earnings power became visible and the multiple began to repair. The base that formed in the final months was shallow — only two contractions — but tight, compressing to 3.0%. It closed the latest session at 63.94, 0.8% below its 64.47 high, with RSI at 59.0 and the RS line at new highs.

analyses.name: Chevron Corporation
analyses.verdict: The disciplined way to own a wartime crude premium — 7.7% of overhead room, 87 days to earnings, and a thesis that inverts on a peace deal.

financials.summary: Chevron's last full fiscal year was dominated by the crude price spike that followed the outbreak of the US-Iran conflict. Upstream realisations rose sharply, and because Chevron's cost base is largely fixed in the short run, the incremental barrel dropped almost entirely to the bottom line — the mechanism behind EPS growth of 322.9% on revenue growth of 52.6%. Permian production continued to grow while capital intensity stayed disciplined, a contrast to prior cycles when high prices triggered overspending. Downstream refining margins were also elevated, adding a second earnings engine. Free cash flow was substantial and management directed it to dividends and buybacks rather than aggressive reinvestment, keeping the balance sheet conservatively geared. The critical question the numbers cannot answer is durability: this is a price-driven result, and the price is a function of a geopolitical conflict.

journey_52w.summary: Chevron's year was shaped by an external event rather than by company execution. The stock traded as low as 144.01 during a period of soft crude and weak refining margins, then re-rated sharply as the Iran conflict removed supply from the market and pushed Brent into the $80-90 range that Goldman now expects to persist until a deal or a major escalation. It reached 209.23 at the peak of war-premium pricing and has since given back some of that, closing the latest session at 193.18 — 7.7% below the high. That pullback is the setup: RSI is 67.1, three-month momentum only +1.4%, and there is real overhead room rather than a breakout to chase. The stock is a direct proxy for the Hormuz negotiation now underway.

analyses.name: Valero Energy Corporation
analyses.verdict: The least extended name sitting at a 52-week high anywhere in the scan — RSI 55 with a 23% three-month trend and 11.2x earnings.

financials.summary: Valero's last full year was exceptional because refining margins, not crude prices, drive its economics — and the Iran conflict widened crack spreads dramatically as product supply tightened faster than crude. That produced EPS growth of 453.5% on revenue growth of 51.7%, the strongest earnings leverage of any energy name in the scan. As a pure-play refiner with a large, complex US Gulf Coast footprint, Valero can process heavier and cheaper crude grades, which widens the differential it captures when light-heavy spreads open up. The renewable diesel and ethanol segments provided diversification, though they remain small relative to traditional refining. Management maintained the pattern of returning the large majority of free cash flow to shareholders through buybacks and dividends rather than building new capacity — appropriate discipline in a business where the last capacity cycle destroyed a decade of returns.

analyses.name: GE Aerospace
analyses.verdict: The strongest industrial trend on the board — +31.7% three-month momentum with RSI still under 59 — and you pay 40.7x for it.

financials.summary: GE Aerospace's last full year as a focused pure-play showed why the conglomerate breakup created value. Revenue grew 21.1% and EPS 19.4%, but the more important detail is the mix: the aftermarket services business — spare parts and maintenance on the installed base of LEAP and CFM56 engines — carries structurally higher margins than original-equipment sales, and it grew faster. That installed base is the moat: engines sold today generate service revenue for decades, giving multi-year visibility that few industrials can match. Commercial air traffic growth drove shop visits and spare-parts demand, while the defence segment provided a stable counterweight. Supply-chain constraints remained the binding limitation on delivering more engines, which paradoxically supported pricing. Free cash flow conversion was strong and management continued returning capital while investing in LEAP production capacity.

analyses.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The answer to whether tech is broken: it isn't — Amazon closed at a 52-week high on 1.88x volume with the strongest TradingView reading of any name I cover.

financials.summary: Amazon's last full fiscal year was a margin story more than a revenue story. Revenue grew 19.6%, but EPS grew 242.3% — the gap is the point. Years of heavy fulfilment-network investment and the regionalisation of the US logistics footprint finally converted into operating leverage as cost-to-serve fell. AWS reaccelerated as enterprise AI workloads moved from experimentation into production, and because cloud carries far higher margins than retail, that mix shift compounded the earnings effect. The advertising business — now a very large, high-margin revenue line — continued growing faster than retail. Against those tailwinds, capital expenditure rose sharply to build AI data-centre capacity, which is the central tension in the story: enormous free cash flow generation running alongside enormous reinvestment. Management has been explicit that the capex is demand-driven rather than speculative.

The advance was driven by the earnings inflection becoming undeniable: as AWS growth reaccelerated and retail margins expanded simultaneously, the market re-rated the whole company. The final move to highs came on 1.88x average volume with a pocket pivot and the relative-strength line at new highs, which is real accumulation. The one structural caveat is that the base is loose — an 11.1% widest contraction — so this is a momentum entry, not a tight-risk one, and the price sits 15% above its 50-DMA.

analyses.name: Alphabet Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cheapest mega-cap growth with the most overhead room — 7.2% below its high at 25.3x, and TradingView's gauge shows zero sell signals.

financials.summary: Alphabet's last full fiscal year combined solid revenue growth of 24.2% with an EPS gain of 294%, a gap driven by margin expansion and a lower comparative base. Search revenue proved far more resilient than the AI-disruption narrative had implied — query volumes and monetisation both held up as AI features were integrated into the results page rather than cannibalising it. YouTube advertising and subscriptions grew steadily. Google Cloud was the standout, reaching meaningful profitability and growing quickly as AI workloads drove demand for TPU capacity and Gemini-based services. Cost discipline instituted in prior years persisted, so operating leverage was real rather than accounting-driven. Capital expenditure rose substantially to fund AI infrastructure, mirroring the industry-wide buildout, and the company continued large-scale buybacks alongside its dividend.

analyses.name: NetApp, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A stock at a 52-week high with RSI 58 and an 18.6x multiple — leadership priced like a value stock, and TradingView shows zero sell signals.

financials.summary: NetApp's last full fiscal year was driven by the all-flash array transition and by AI infrastructure demand pulling enterprise storage back into growth. Revenue grew 12.5% and EPS 23.4% — the earnings outpacing revenue because all-flash and the public-cloud storage services carry better margins than the legacy disk-based business they replace. The AI connection is direct and often underappreciated: training and inference workloads require high-throughput storage adjacent to compute, and enterprises building private AI infrastructure need exactly the kind of data platform NetApp sells. Recurring revenue from support contracts and cloud subscriptions continued to grow as a share of the total, improving revenue quality and visibility. analyses.name: DexCom, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The strongest healthcare breakout in the scan — new high on 1.81x volume with a pocket pivot, 87 days to earnings, and TradingView's best possible gauge.

financials.summary: DexCom's last full year saw revenue grow 13.1% and EPS 43.6% as continuous glucose monitoring continued penetrating both the type 1 and, more importantly, the much larger type 2 diabetes population. Margin expansion outpaced revenue because the sensor business benefits from manufacturing scale — each incremental sensor produced at higher volume costs less — and because the newer product generations carry better economics. Reimbursement coverage broadened during the year, particularly for type 2 patients not on intensive insulin therapy, which structurally expands the addressable market. International expansion contributed growth at lower initial margins. The competitive picture with Abbott remained intense, and the emergence of GLP-1 drugs introduced a genuine strategic question about long-term diabetes management that the company addressed by positioning CGM as complementary to, rather than displaced by, pharmacological treatment.

analyses.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
analyses.verdict: How to own AI infrastructure while the semiconductors are broken — contracted data-centre demand, revenue +29.9%, and a perfect TradingView gauge.

financials.summary: Digital Realty's last full year was defined by data-centre leasing demand running well ahead of available supply. Revenue grew 29.9% as AI training and inference workloads consumed capacity faster than the industry could build it, and — critically for a landlord — this demand arrives as multi-year contracted leases rather than as transactional revenue. Releasing spreads on expiring leases turned sharply positive, meaning existing capacity is being repriced upward, which is the highest-quality form of REIT growth. Power availability, not construction capital, became the binding constraint on the industry, which advantaged incumbents with secured grid interconnections. The reported EPS of -58.7% requires context: REIT accounting charges large depreciation against heavy development spending, so GAAP earnings substantially understate cash generation — funds from operations is the metric the sector is valued on. Development capital expenditure was elevated, funded through a mix of joint ventures, asset recycling and equity.

analyses.verdict: The cheapest name in my STRONG BUY tier at 10.9x, with contracted government revenue that ignores both the Iran headline and the rate path.

financials.summary: SAIC's last full fiscal year produced EPS growth of 83.8% on revenue growth of just 1.5% — a gap that tells you exactly what kind of story this is. The earnings gain came from margin improvement and share repurchase, not from demand expansion: the company shifted its contract mix away from low-margin pass-through work toward higher-value systems integration and digital-modernisation programmes, and it retired a meaningful share count. Government IT services revenue is contracted and appropriated, which makes it unusually predictable but also caps growth to budget cycles and recompete outcomes. Backlog and book-to-bill are the metrics that matter more than reported revenue, since they determine the following years. Free cash flow conversion was strong and management prioritised buybacks over acquisitions, which at a low double-digit multiple is a rational allocation of capital.

analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING — the 31.5 score means 'no trading history', not 'sell'; but down 45.8% from its post-IPO high with first earnings tomorrow, this is a hold-don't-add.

financials.period: FY2025 (ended Dec 2025) — first full year as a public reporting company
financials.summary: SpaceX comes to public markets with two businesses of very different character. The launch business is effectively a monopoly in commercial orbital launch: reusable boosters have driven cost per kilogram to orbit far below any competitor, and the customer base spans commercial satellite operators, NASA and national-security programmes with multi-year contracted awards. The second business, Starlink, is a consumer and enterprise broadband subscription service — recurring revenue with far better scaling economics than launch, but requiring enormous upfront capital to build and continuously replenish the satellite constellation. Reported revenue growth of 15.4% understates the divergence between a mature launch cadence and a still-scaling subscriber base. The capital intensity is the central financial fact: constellation replenishment is a permanent, large capital expenditure line, and the 126.8x forward multiple means the market is pricing years of flawless execution on Starlink subscriber growth. Because this is the company's first period as a public reporter, comparability and disclosure quality are still being established.

critical.valuation: At 126.8x forward earnings, valuation is the entire debate. The bull case is that Starlink becomes a global broadband utility with recurring revenue and that launch monopoly economics persist — a combination that could justify almost any multiple if execution holds. The bear case is that the price already assumes that outcome, leaving no margin for the satellite-replenishment capex cycle, a launch failure, or competitive entry. For holders: the franchise case is intact and the stock is deeply oversold at RSI 29.7, but adding ahead of a first earnings report with no trading history is not a calculated risk, it is a guess.
